channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: Issue fields are now generally available
item.description: Issue fields are now generally available for all GitHub organizations on Free, Team, Enterprise, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency plans and will ship in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23. Issue fields bring structured, typed metadata to issues, making it easy to track priority, effort, dates, and custom values consistently across your organization.

item.title: Cost centers now support AI credit pools
item.description: You can now cap how much of your enterprise’s monthly included AI credits a cost center can use. This is available through the REST API today.

item.title: The latest AI news we announced in June 2026
item.description: Here are Google’s latest AI updates from June 2026.

item.title: Set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and SDK
item.description: You can now set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot SDK to cap the amount an agent spends in a session. This is especially useful for automation, where no one is actively monitoring the agent’s work.

item.title: New C++ language server config skill for Copilot CLI
item.description: The Microsoft C++ Language Server is now available as a plugin on the Copilot Plugins marketplace. It includes a new built-in setup skill that helps automate project setup, making it easier to generate and maintain the compile_commands.json file the language server needs to understand your code.

item.title: Kimi K2.7 Code is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Kimi K2.7 Code, an open-weight model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. This is the first open-weight model offered as a selectable option in the Copilot model picker, giving you more choice and a lower-cost option for your coding workflows.

item.title: GitHub Models is being fully retired on July 30, 2026
item.description: In June, we announced that we are retiring GitHub Models and closed it to new customers. We’re now sharing the timeline for the next step: GitHub Models will be fully retired on July 30, 2026.

item.title: Enterprises can default to auto model selection
item.description: Enterprise administrators can now set model to auto in the enterprise managed-settings.json to make Copilot auto model selection the default for new conversations. Add auto to.github-private/.github/copilot/managed-settings.json in your source organization for enterprise governance so new conversations start with Copilot auto model selection by default.

item.title: Enterprise managed-settings.json is generally available
item.description: GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can configure AI standards through a managed-settings.json file maintained in a.github-private repository in a selected organization. This allows the enterprise to define new governance and extensibility flows that apply to Copilot clients such as VS Code or Copilot CLI.

item.title: Copilot vision is generally available
item.description: Copilot vision is now generally available. You can attach images and PDFs directly to your chat prompts so Copilot can reason about what it sees alongside your code.

item.title: Copilot CLI auto model selection routes based on task
item.description: Editor’s note (July 1, 2026): Updated the premium request costs to reference AI credits. GitHub Copilot auto model selection now routes to the best model for your task in Copilot CLI, using utilization and model health metrics for a high quality, reliable, and token-efficient experience.

item.title: Browser tools for GitHub Copilot in VS Code are generally available
item.description: Editor’s note (July 1, 2026): Added more detail about which permissions stay under your control and the existing network domain controls. Browser tools for GitHub Copilot in VS Code are now generally available.

item.title: our statement
item.description: We've restored access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. See our statement for more information.

item.title: Introducing GeneBench-Pro
item.description: Introducing GeneBench-Pro, a new benchmark testing AI performance in genomics, biology, and scientific research using complex, real-world datasets.

item.title: How ChatGPT adoption has expanded
item.description: New OpenAI Signals data shows how ChatGPT adoption is growing globally, with users increasing usage, exploring more capabilities, and driving growth across regions and languages.

item.title: Core dump epidemiology: fixing an 18-year-old bug
item.description: OpenAI engineers used large-scale core dump analysis to debug rare infrastructure crashes, uncovering both a hardware fault and a long-standing software bug.

item.title: Inside Genebench-Pro
item.description: Inside Genebench-Pro

item.title: Start building with Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash
item.description: Start building with Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash

item.title: Per-user AI credit budgets available for cost centers
item.description: Enterprise admins can now set a cost center user-level budget: one per-user AI credit budget on a cost center that applies to every individual in it. As membership changes, the budget follows.

item.title: Copilot Agent is now available in JetBrains AI Assistant
item.description: Today, JetBrains and GitHub are announcing a deeper integration between JetBrains AI Assistant and GitHub Copilot. Millions of developers already rely on the GitHub Copilot plugin as their AI pair programmer in JetBrains IDEs, and Copilot has also been available inside JetBrains AI Assistant through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5 is generally available for GitHub Copilot
item.description: Claude Sonnet 5 is Anthropic’s latest Sonnet-class model, now available in GitHub Copilot. It brings strong coding performance to everyday development and agentic workflows, giving developers a new Sonnet-class option for tasks across the IDE and CLI.

item.title: Subscribe to webhooks
item.description: Webhooks for Claude Managed Agents now cover the agent, deployment, and deployment run lifecycle. You can react to a newly published agent version, a paused deployment, or a failed scheduled run without polling. See the Agent events, Deployment events, and Deployment run events tabs in Subscribe to webhooks.

item.title: injection_location
item.description: Claude Managed Agents vaults now support an injection_location setting on environment variable credentials (the Environment variable tab). It controls whether the credential's value is substituted, at egress, into the agent's outbound request headers, the request body, or both.

item.title: agent
item.description: When creating a Claude Managed Agents session, you can now override the agent's configuration for that session. Pass agent with type: "agent_with_overrides" to replace the model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, or skills for a single session. The agent itself is unchanged.

item.title: GET /v1/sessions
item.description: Listing sessions for Claude Managed Agents now supports backward pagination. GET /v1/sessions returns a prev_page cursor alongside next_page; pass it as the page parameter to return to the previous page. See Pagination.

item.title: Redeploying Claude Fable 5
item.description: Anthropic is redeploying Claude Fable 5 starting July 1 following the lifting of export controls, with updated cybersecurity safeguards and a new industry jailbreak framework.

item.title: event_deltas[]
item.description: Claude Managed Agents session event streams now support event deltas. Opt in with the event_deltas[] query parameter on GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream. The event_start and event_delta events preview an agent message's text as it's generated, before the complete agent.message event arrives.

item.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
item.description: Our most agentic Sonnet yet, with top-tier intelligence for coding and everyday professional work.

item.title: Claude Science, an AI workbench for scientists
item.description: Claude Science is a customizable app that integrates the tools and packages researchers most often use, produces auditable artifacts, and provides flexible access to computing resources.

item.title: Mapping Europe’s AI Workforce Opportunity
item.description: A new OpenAI report maps how AI could reshape jobs across the EU, highlighting which occupations may face automation, growth, or workflow changes.

item.title: Restrict issue creation to collaborators only
item.description: Repository admins can now restrict issue creation to collaborators with write access. This gives you more control over who can open issues and helps reduce unwanted issue creation, while keeping issue workflows available to the people who actively maintain and contribute to the project.

item.title: Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) is now in preview for GitHub Copilot
item.description: Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) is now rolling out in preview on GitHub Copilot. Fast mode delivers significantly faster output token speeds while maintaining the same intelligence as Claude Opus 4.8, making it well suited for interactive coding and agentic workflows where responsiveness matters.

item.title: claude-opus-4-6
item.description: We've removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.6. Requests to claude-opus-4-6 with speed: "fast" no longer run at fast speed or premium pricing: they run at standard speed, are billed at standard rates, and do not return an error. The response's usage.speed field reports the speed used. To continue using fast mode, migrate to Claude Opus 4.8. Read more in Fast mode.

item.title: HP Inc. launches Frontier strategic partnership with OpenAI
item.description: HP Inc. scales its OpenAI Frontier partnership to deploy AI across customer experiences, software development, and enterprise operations.

item.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
item.description: OpenAI previews GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model with stronger capabilities in coding, science, and cybersecurity, paired with its most advanced safety stack.

item.title: Track total merges by adoption phase in enterprise and organization reports
item.description: Building on the AI adoption phase cohorts added to the Copilot usage metrics API, organization and enterprise reports now report the total number of pull requests merged by each adoption phase. What’s new The totals_by_ai_adoption_phase breakdown previously reported per-user averages only.

item.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise
item.description: MAI-Code-1-Flash, Microsoft AI’s in-house coding model, is now generally available for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise, building on its recent expansion across Copilot surfaces. Purpose-built for coding and optimized for GitHub Copilot, MAI-Code-1-Flash delivers fast, low-latency responses that make it well-suited for high-volume, iterative agentic coding workflows where speed and efficiency matter most.

item.title: GitHub Desktop 3.6: Worktrees and deeper Copilot integration
item.description: GitHub Desktop 3.6 brings more of your day-to-day Git flow into one place with GitHub Copilot now powering commit authoring and merge conflict resolution, plus new Git worktree support. The problem More and more development happens with the help of AI and coding agents, which raises the bar for the everyday Git moments in between.

item.title: rate limits
item.description: We've raised rate limits across the Claude API. Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku rate limits now match Claude Opus at every usage tier, and usage tiers have been consolidated into three: Start, Build, and Scale. Most organizations move to a higher tier, no organization receives lower limits than before, and no action is required. You can view your tier and current limits in the Claude Console.

item.title: How agents are transforming work
item.description: A new OpenAI research paper shows how AI agents are transforming work, enabling longer, more complex tasks and expanding productivity across roles.

item.title: GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available
item.description: GitHub Copilot for Jira is now generally available. Since launching the public preview in March 2026, we have shipped a series of enhancements based on your feedback, including model selection, Confluence context via MCP, custom agents, custom fields, space-level guidance, and review request notifications in Jira.

item.title: Enterprise-managed settings now support strictKnownMarketplaces in VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description: Enterprises can now control which plugins their users can install in GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code. This setting is now available in public preview.

item.title: Copilot code review: Analysis depth and efficiency updates
item.description: Copilot code review now uses the built-in file exploration tools available in the Copilot CLI and SDK, significantly improving review cost efficiency with no change to your existing workflow. If you’re in the Medium analysis depth public preview, you’ll also see some new updates centered around configurability and visibility of review depth.

item.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip
item.description: OpenAI and Broadcom introduce Jalapeño, a custom AI chip built for LLM inference to improve performance, efficiency, and scale across AI systems.

item.title: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
item.description: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash

item.title: Changes to model selection for Free and Student plans
item.description: Copilot Free and Student plans will now use Copilot auto model selection as the default and only model selection experience. Auto dynamically selects the best model for each task, removing the need for manual choice.

item.title: How Omio is building the future of conversational travel
item.description: Discover how Omio uses OpenAI to power conversational travel experiences, accelerate product development, and transform into an AI-native company.

item.title: Helping build shared standards for advanced AI
item.description: OpenAI helps build shared standards for advanced AI, supporting evaluation frameworks, safety practices, and global cooperation through the Appia Foundation.

item.title: Safety dashboard
item.description: Released the Safety Usage Dashboard on the OpenAI API platform. The Safety dashboard shows blocked Responses requests based on safety_identifier values sent on requests to identify end users.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app support for BYOK
item.description: The GitHub Copilot app now supports bring your own key (BYOK), so you can run agent sessions against your own model providers, including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic, LM Studio, Ollama, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Add a provider in Settings → Model Providers with your endpoint and API key, or just a host for LM Studio or Ollama.
